question: M45's verdict made its minimal-model no-go conditional on a real Bistritzer-MacDonald evaluation.  Does TMD-proximitised nodal MATBG (Biswas-Sensarma-Randeria order parameters, induced Ising SOC) have odd Sato-Fujimoto Chern parity (-1)^nu at any honest point when evaluated at the physical moire-BZ TRIM (Gamma_m + 3 M_m) on the validated BM flat bands -- per valley, for the physical inter-valley pairing, and for a valley-polarised control?

MODEL_CHOICES.bm_hamiltonian: m1/bm.py REUSED verbatim (theta = 1.025 deg, hbar vF = 620 meV nm, wAB = 110 meV, wAA/wAB = 0.8) -- the repo's validated module (paper/M1_REPORT.md).  Production BdG at basis_shells N = 3 (Ng = 49); parity convergence checked against N = (2, 4) below.  Flat-band edges at N=3 (12x12 BZ grid): [-1.4613, 1.4613] meV, W = 2.9226 meV vs production 2.9220 meV.
MODEL_CHOICES.trims: the four physical TRIM of the moire BZ: Gamma_m and three M_m.  Representatives registered as minimal-|G_Q|, minimal-|k*| images (trim_data); valley- blocks are built at frame momentum -k* via the exact TRS identity h_-(-k*) = P h_+(k*)^* P (P: g -> -g), so the two valleys' normal spectra agree to machine precision by construction.
MODEL_CHOICES.ising_soc: valley-odd Zeeman-like: +lambda_I s_z in valley +, -lambda_I s_z in valley -; spin is a doubling of the BM basis.  Rashba omitted: M40 6(i)/M45 closed it, and the parity question here is Ising-driven; graphene Rashba would add a k-independent spin-orbit block -- flagged as not evaluated.
MODEL_CHOICES.chemical_potential: mu = E_lo(N) + E_F with E_F measured from the LOWER flat-band edge at lambda_I = 0 (registered; the gate fixes density, not mu -- not modelled).
MODEL_CHOICES.pairing_implementation: LOCAL pairing in the plane-wave basis (layer- and sublattice-diagonal, partner map fixed by momentum conservation), amplitude = the stated Biswas form factor at the pair's crystal momentum, CHOSEN OVER flat-band projection because (i) it keeps particle-hole symmetry exact in the full shell basis (PHS residual is identically zero by construction, benchmark iv), (ii) for INTER-valley pairing the flat-band projection of this operator is EXACTLY the Biswas Delta(k) with unit form factor (TRS: the overlap between a flat state and the T-image of its partner is 1 -- verified numerically in projection_factors), so no projection error arises in the physical arm; (iii) for INTRA-valley pairing the flat-band projection factor < 1 is REPORTED, not hidden.
MODEL_CHOICES.d_wave: real singlet, Delta(p) = Delta2 (|p| a_m)^2 cos(2 theta_p - 2 beta), Delta0 = 0 forced (Biswas et al., M40 Sec 6); p measured from Gamma_m (the IKS pocket lives there); a_m = 13.751 nm.  FLAG: at the M_m TRIM |p| a_m = 2pi/sqrt(3) so (|p| a_m)^2 = 13.16 -- the small-k form is EXTRAPOLATED there (values in trim_data); a periodised first-star harmonic with identical small-k limit is run as a robustness variant (harmonic_robustness).
MODEL_CHOICES.triplet_p: triplet, k-independent d-vector (polar, d || z): f = Delta_p sin(p . a_1) (first moire harmonic; ANY odd periodic form factor vanishes at ALL four TRIM, so at the TRIM the parity is blind to the lobe direction AND to the d-vector orientation -- same structural flag as M45).
MODEL_CHOICES.beta: beta = 0 registered; swept {0, pi/8, pi/4} on a sub-grid (beta_sweep)
MODEL_CHOICES.delta_amplitude: 0.05-0.3 meV grid (Park scale 0.159 meV); for the triplet the TRIM values vanish identically so the amplitude grid is run for the d-wave only (triplet at 0.159; verified f(TRIM) = 0)
MODEL_CHOICES.arm_a: intra-valley pairing per valley block (M45 construction on the real bands), pair momentum 2*Gamma_m per valley (pocket-centred); total = product of per-valley parities
MODEL_CHOICES.arm_b: INTER-valley pairing (the physical case): one combined BdG, electron sector = valley+ (+ valley-), pairing psi+_{k,s} chi-_{-k,s'}, PHS acts across valleys
MODEL_CHOICES.arm_c: CONTROL, NOT PHYSICAL: pairing in valley+ only, valley- unpaired; bounds what valley polarisation would buy; excluded at nu = -2 by IKS evidence (spin-degenerate pocket) and by Biswas et al.
MODEL_CHOICES.iks_flag: the IKS reconstruction itself (C2 incommensurate Kekule spiral order) is NOT in the BM Hamiltonian: this evaluation runs on the BARE BM bands.  If parity comes out odd anywhere, the IKS-reconstructed normal state is the remaining step before any claim.
MODEL_CHOICES.pfaffian: M45's validated real-Schur routine reproduced verbatim (attribution in code) + overflow-safe sign/log variant + Householder-tridiagonalisation Pfaffian for the large matrices, cross-validated against Schur on random AND sampled physics matrices (pfaffian_selftest, pf_cross_check).
MODEL_CHOICES.normalisation: each per-TRIM sign is divided by the sign of a deep-trivial reference of the same dimension, making per-TRIM factors convention-free (trivial = +1) and the four-TRIM product basis-independent.

benchmark_ii_zero_pairing.criterion: Delta=0, lambda_I=h_x=0: normalised per-TRIM factor +1 everywhere (even parity, all arms)

benchmark_iii_swave_no_soc.criterion: s-wave, lambda_I=0, h_x=0: parity +1 per TRIM, all arms, all amplitudes, all E_F

beta_sweep.note: beta rotates the d-wave lobes; at beta = pi/4 the form factor vanishes at the M3 TRIM, so beta CAN in principle move the parity when a pair-breaking field competes with the M-point gap -- any dependence found is reported, not suppressed

benchmark_iv_phs_residual.note: PHS is exact by construction (antisymmetric Delta, hole block = -(A - mu)^T); residual is float roundoff

valley_image_check.statement: M45's cancellation theorem premise, tested on the real BM bands: at every TRIM the valley- BdG block should carry the same per-TRIM Pfaffian sign as the valley+ block, so the two-valley product is a perfect square.  On the BM bands the two blocks are related by the ANTIUNITARY composition (TRS x spin rotation), not by a plain spin rotation as on M45's square lattice -- and antiunitary equivalence does NOT protect individual Pfaffian signs.  RESULT: the per-TRIM image property is BROKEN (violations listed); at beta = 0 the violations always flip the M1 and M2 signs TOGETHER (the beta = 0 d-wave has f(M1) = f(M2), an accidental mirror), so the per-valley PRODUCTS still coincide and the beta = 0 grid shows no odd two-valley total.  At generic beta the mirror is gone and the two-valley intra-valley parity DOES go odd (generic_beta_map) -- M45's cancellation theorem is FALSE on the real bands as a theorem, and the window closure must (and does) rest on the physical inter-valley channel instead.

verdict.verdict: M45 CONFIRMED on BM bands -- window closed, load-bearing
verdict.qualifier: The closure does NOT rest on M45's valley-cancellation theorem: that theorem is FALSE on the real BM bands.  The per-TRIM valley image property is broken (8 violations at beta = 0, products saved only by the accidental beta = 0 M1<->M2 mirror), and at generic beta (pi/8) the two-valley INTRA-valley parity goes odd at 13 honest grid points (N=4- and Schur-verified).  What closes the physical window is the inter-valley structure itself: valley-odd Ising SOC enters an inter-valley BdG as a spin-dependent shift of BOTH pair members (Ising protection), the TRIM state counts stay Kramers-doubled across the valleys, and arm b is EVEN at every grid point, every beta, both order parameters, both form-factor variants, and in every benchmark limit.
verdict.control_note: control-arm odd points where the odd factor comes from the UNPAIRED valley are Fermi-count parities of a gapless subsystem, not usable topology; the meaningful bound is the points where the PAIRED valley itself is odd (recorded per-factor in arm_c rows).

HONESTY: (1) evaluated on the BARE BM bands: the IKS reconstruction (C2 incommensurate Kekule spiral) that defines the actual nu=-2-delta normal state is NOT in the Hamiltonian.  The Biswas order parameters are classified FROM the IKS state; using them on bare BM bands is the registered inconsistency of this module, and an IKS-reconstructed normal state is the remaining step if any parity here (or in a follow-up) comes out odd.

(2) the d-wave continuum form factor is an extrapolation at the M_m TRIM ((|p| a_m)^2 = 13.16 there); the periodised-harmonic robustness arm quantifies the sensitivity (harmonic_robustness.n_disagreements).

(3) intra-valley pairing (arm a) drops pairing partners for outer-shell plane waves at the M TRIM (counts in trim_data); these states sit hundreds of meV from E_F, never cross a threshold on this grid, and the lambda_I = 0 rows anchor the even baseline; the N-convergence check bounds the residual effect.
(4) mu is fixed relative to the lambda_I = 0 flat-band edge; a gate fixes density, not mu.  No self-consistency of Delta.

(5) Rashba admixture is omitted (closed by M40 6(i)/M45); note that in the BM plane-wave basis graphene Rashba is k-independent and would NOT vanish at the TRIM -- reopening it would need the measured Rashba scale, which M40 records as negligible.
(6) the beta sweep and amplitude grid are parity look-up tables, not free-energy minimisations: which beta / amplitude nature picks is outside this module.
(7) vortex-level interpretation (odd parity => odd number of stable vortex Majoranas) is exactly Sato-Fujimoto's theorem; nothing here is a device claim.

(8) the load-bearing closure is CONDITIONAL on the pairing being inter-valley (the Biswas/IKS reading).  The same calculation shows that an intra-valley (PDW) or valley-polarised pairing WOULD reach odd parity at honest parameters (arm a at generic beta; arm c) -- so any future evidence for valley-polarised pairing in MATBG reopens the question through that door, not through Ising SOC on inter-valley pairs.
